import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset from the specified path
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Drop rows with missing income, as it's crucial for this analysis
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Feature Engineering: Create total spending and household size columns
mnt_cols = [col for col in df.columns if 'Mnt' in col]
df['TotalSpending'] = df[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)
df['ChildrenCount'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']

# Filter out extreme income outliers for better visualization of the main data distribution
df_filtered = df[(df['Income'] < 200000) & (df['Income'] > 0)]

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid", {'axes.grid': True, 'grid.linestyle': '--', 'grid.color': '0.9'})
sns.set_context("notebook", font_scale=1.2)

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a scatter plot showing the relationship between Income and Total Spending,
# colored by the number of children in the household.
palette = sns.color_palette("viridis_r", n_colors=df_filtered['ChildrenCount'].nunique())

scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='Income',
    y='TotalSpending',
    hue='ChildrenCount',
    palette=palette,
    alpha=0.7,
    s=70,
    edgecolor='w',
    linewidth=0.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Annotations ---
# Set title and labels with clear, descriptive text
ax.set_title('Customer Spending by Income and Household Size', fontsize=20, pad=20, weight='bold', color='#333333')
ax.set_xlabel('Annual Household Income', fontsize=14, labelpad=15, color='#333333')
ax.set_ylabel('Total Spending (All Product Categories)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15, color='#333333')

# Format axes to be more readable (e.g., thousands with 'k')
ax.get_xaxis().set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x/1000:.0f}k'))
ax.get_yaxis().set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x/1000:.0f}k'))
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12, colors='#555555')

# Improve the legend
legend = ax.get_legend()
legend.set_title('Number of Children')
plt.setp(legend.get_title(), fontsize='13', weight='bold')

# Add an annotation to highlight a key trend
ax.annotate(
    'Spending generally increases with income.\nHowever, for a given income level,\nhouseholds with more children tend to spend less.',
    xy=(80000, 500),
    xytext=(100000, 1500),
    arrowprops=dict(facecolor='black', arrowstyle='->', connectionstyle="arc3,rad=0.1"),
    fontsize=12,
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.5", fc="aliceblue", ec="k", lw=1, alpha=0.8)
)

# Set plot area background color and remove top/right spines for a cleaner look
ax.set_facecolor('#f5f5f5')
sns.despine(ax=ax, trim=True)

# Save the figure with specified settings
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
